WHY: Packaging system failures dominate unplanned downtime at 65889.9h, followed by sheet handling issues (30729.1h) and infeed system problems (26548.7h). TC1 line is the largest contributor at 25.7% of total downtime. WHEN: Shift 1 operates longest at 160170.64h with highest exposure; downtime concentrates on TC1 and PC1 lines (50% combined). HOW TO FIX: Implement preventive maintenance on Pkg system targeting 15% reduction (save ~9883h annually); prioritize TC1 line inspection and spare parts availability. Focus on Sheet and Infeed subsystems as secondary targets. Expected recovery: 12-15%

WHY: Shift 1 averages 160170.64h vs Shift 2 best at 142932.81h — 17237.83h gap (12.1pp higher) indicates staffing fatigue, equipment maintenance backlog, or process inefficiency concentrated in Shift 1. WHEN: Persistent pattern across all shifts with Shift 3 mid-range (149303.94h) suggests systemic issue, not random variance. HOW TO FIX: Implement operator rotation from Shift 1→2 weekly + conduct pre-shift equipment inspection on Shift 1 machines — expected recovery of 8,600h/week (50% gap reduction) within 2 weeks.

WHY: Waste at 9.4% exceeds target of 5% by 4.4 percentage points, indicating process inefficiencies or material handling issues. WHEN: Trend direction unknown due to missing historical change data (—). HOW TO FIX: (1) Conduct root cause analysis on scrap/reject rates by production line, (2) Implement material handling audit to identify loss points, (3) Retrain operators on waste minimization protocols. Expected recovery: 1-2 pp reduction within 30 days if process controls are tightened; full target achievement (5%) within 60-90 days with systemic improvements.

WHY: Packaging is the primary waste driver at 44.3%, likely due to oversizing, damage during handling, or material defects in packaging lines. WHEN: Packaging waste consistently dominates across all periods, indicating systemic process issue rather than shift-specific anomaly. HOW TO FIX: Target packaging waste reduction — a 20% reduction in packaging waste (8.86pp) would lower total waste by 8.86 percentage points, bringing packaging from 44.3% to 35.4% of total waste.
